speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our goal is simple and unchanged: to create more opportunities for Singaporeans, at every level of the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: At its core, economic development is human capital development.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is the skills, knowledge and ingenuity of a country's people that generate economic prosperity.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Businesses attract talent with these attributes, local and global.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And talent and the teams they develop around them in turn attract more businesses and encourages them to grow higher value-added activities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Countries that manage to develop and anchor talent benefit from this virtuous cycle, which benefits everyone in the workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Those that do not, stagnate and worse, fall behind.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Getting this right is all the more critical for Singapore, where people are our only real resource.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Many countries know this and they are playing an offensive game.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They have populations larger than ours, but they are still going out of their way to court global talent.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Prime Minister mentioned Germany and the UK in his National Day Rally speech.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Australia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) have also launched talent visas of their own.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And within the last month, countries much nearer to us such as Malaysia and Thailand have done the same.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I do not think that it is mere coincidence that countries and even cities around the world have upped their game to attract global talent.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They know that when it comes to talent, you can never have enough – because of the virtuous cycle that I talked about.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In this race, Singapore is coming from a position of strength, but we cannot stand still.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As we move to create a high value, inclusive and a more sustainable economy, there are many opportunities for us to capture, be it in the green sector, in AI, or in fintech.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And to do that, we need to attract the best from around the world, even as we do our utmost to develop local talents in each field.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These are the rainmakers of the world, whom we hope to bring to Singapore, so that we can tap on their networks.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We can grow teams around them and learn from their expertise, and through these efforts, we can level up our industries as well as our workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The questions raised on the recent enhancements to the work pass framework – across 24 Parliamentary Questions – generally seek more details on the targeted enhancements to attract global talent and our ongoing efforts to develop our own local talent pipeline.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These are important and valid questions and I thank Members for them.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As part of my Ministerial Statement today, I will address oral Question Nos 1 to 18 from today's Order Paper as well as questions filed by Miss Rachel Ong, Mr Patrick Tay, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim and Mr Don Wee for the sitting on or after 13 September.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They are aimed at attracting top talent in diverse fields and experienced tech professionals in areas of skill shortages.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They build on our efforts to improve the complementarity and diversity of our foreign workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The enhancements will also aim to build significant first-mover and sustainable competitive advantages in new growth areas to keep us ahead of the competition.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I will address questions raised on each move in turn.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: On the ONE Pass, Members have sought clarifications on the privileges, criteria, safeguards, expected numbers as well as impact on local employment outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai has asked what would make the ONE Pass more attractive to talent, compared to the Tech.Pass.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Similar to the Tech.Pass, the ONE Pass is a personalised pass that allows the holder to concurrently start, operate and work for multiple companies in Singapore at any one time.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Spouses of ONE Pass holders are also able to obtain a Letter of Consent (LOC) to work.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In response to Assoc Prof Jamus Lim's question, we do not have restrictions on the occupations that LOC holders can work in – this is, generally, the same approach for all other work pass holders, including dependants working in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The longer duration of the pass as well as the LOC for spouses, is meant to give top talent the additional assurance they need when deciding whether to come to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Businesses tell us that these are key factors that top talent consider before deciding where to go.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Some Members asked why dependants of ONE Pass holders are able to work on an LOC instead of being assessed based on their own merits.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Today, dependants of EP holders are eligible to work in Singapore if they obtain a work pass.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We stopped issuing LOCs to dependants, not because we did not want them to work here, but because it made sense to hold them to a similar bar as all other foreigners.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But when we are talking about top talent, we must be mindful of how global and mobile they are and how stiff the competition is for them.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Many other jurisdictions, including Hong Kong, the UAE and the UK, offer work privileges for dependants.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: When people make major relocation decisions, it is usually a family decision.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Without certainty for the spouse, these talents may choose to go elsewhere.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In terms of numbers, it is not that material.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Of the top 5% of existing EP holders that might qualify for the ONE Pass as a proxy, only a small minority have spouses who are working.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But in terms of the signal that we are giving to top talent, it is absolutely material and absolutely needle-moving.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In gist, we are looking at individuals who have demonstrated exceptionally high levels of achievement in the fields of arts, sports, science and academia who can help us push new frontiers, draw in greater investments and interest to grow our local ecosystem and, most importantly, create a very diverse range of opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In the case of sports, for example, it would include current and former world-class, top-ranked athletes who may wish to set up their commercial operations or training bases in Singapore, from which our own local athletes, coaches and sports ecosystem can benefit.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MOM will work with sector agencies that are experts in these domains, such as MCCY, NAC, MOE and NRF, to identify such exceptional talent.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Others, such as Mr Gerald Giam, asked whether the $30,000 fixed monthly salary criterion can be drawn from multiple employers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This helps us ensure that the candidate has played or will be playing a meaningful role in a company.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I think most people would agree with me that $30,000 is, indeed, a high bar, but some worry that there could be potential abuse of the new ONE Pass.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Desmond Choo, Ms He Ting Ru, Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Yip Hon Weng have all asked about the checks that would be in place to prevent abuse or fraudulent applications.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In general, the vast majority of employers and businesses are honest.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They take our policies and MOM seriously and they know that there are grave consequences if they submit a false declaration.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Nevertheless, we will take precautions as we roll out this new pass that offers more privileges and put in safeguards at two levels.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: First level – we will carefully vet all applications.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Today, MOM already conducts back-end checks to sieve out potential cases of false salary declarations.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This includes scrutinising applications from companies with a limited track record and asking for more documents to verify that the salary declared will, in fact, be paid.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will also be applied to all ONE Pass applications.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For those seeking to convert from an existing EP, we will scrutinise their personal income tax filings with IRAS to ensure they are consistent with their applications.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For overseas candidates, we will further assess their company's market capitalisation and revenue based on verifiable sources.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The economic agencies will support MOM in this endeavour.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Second level – we will engage ONE Pass holders during their time in Singapore so that we will be up to date with their professional activities and annual income.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will factor into our assessment on their eligibility for renewals.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms Hazel Poa asked why we do not impose a time limit requiring ONE Pass applicants to remain employed.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The ONE Pass is not meant to be abused as a visit or travel document.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MOM reserves the right to cancel the Pass if there are extended periods of economic inactivity with no good reasons.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Having said that, we are bringing in these talents and giving them flexibilities because we want to encourage them to take risks, to explore new frontiers and to make a big impact to benefit Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is important to allow them some ramp-up period for that to happen and not be too quick to jump to the conclusion that they are not contributing.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Members have asked how many individuals we are expecting to qualify for the ONE Pass.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This Pass is meant for talent that is comparable to the top 5% of our EP holders, which means that the salary criterion is based on the 95th percentile of EP wages.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But the focus is really not on the numbers because our focus is on quality rather than quantity.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: If we impose a quota, we are, essentially, putting a hard limit on how strongly we can compete at the high-end of the global economy.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This ultimately hurts Singaporeans, who will then have fewer opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is the same reason why we do not impose a quota for EPs, but focus instead on setting a high quality bar.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: However, Members would know that we are talking about the top of the pyramid of talent.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Given the highly selective nature of the scheme, there is no risk of a deluge of people coming in through the ONE Pass.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: There are naturally questions on how the ONE Pass would benefit Singaporeans and what the expected impact on local employment is going to be.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Ang Wei Neng have asked this.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim have also asked how meaningful contributions and the success of the ONE Pass will be measured.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As I have mentioned earlier, we will engage all ONE Pass holders.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will allow us to better gauge if they have been contributing in meaningful ways.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Even so, the relationship between talent, innovation and economic growth is more than a simple, linear one.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The contributions of talented individuals go beyond a set of key performance indicators (KPIs).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Limiting and reducing it to that risks constraining us to a measurement and missing the forest for the trees.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Some ONE Pass holders may be employees, making it possible to bring a new business unit to Singapore or grow a new line of business.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Others may set up companies of their own, generating employment as well as supporting their network of business partners who can also provide good jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Yet others may be here to teach, to advise or to consult for local enterprises, sharing their expertise with Singaporean business owners and professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Like any portfolio, the contribution of each ONE Pass holder can vary.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Indeed, not all may succeed in the first instance because such is the nature of risk-taking.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: What matters is the sum of the parts and how well the entire portfolio performs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We are building a rich network of markets, people and ideas that, over time, will show up in the dynamism of our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And if, at the macro level, local job creation remains strong, unemployment low, real income growth sustained, and if, amongst our people, there is always a sense of hope and of opportunities, then I think we would have succeeded.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our local SMEs will benefit from this too.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Don Wee asked how these enhancements to our work pass framework would help our SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They too will be able to benefit from the recent enhancements.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Lennon Tan, President of the Singapore Manufacturing Federation, agrees.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In an interview with Channel 8 news, he mentioned that SMEs can now benefit from the expertise of these talent and professionals as they are not tied to just one employer.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Indeed, some SMEs could benefit from directly hiring the ONE Pass holders, while others could tap on the Pass holder’s expertise through consulting services, or inviting them to join their Boards.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Just as importantly, a vibrant, growing economy will create more business opportunities or build a new eco-system for our SMEs who may be partners, contractors, suppliers or service providers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This may be in up-and-coming sectors like green economy or fintech, where there will be new cheese for our SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Moving on to the new benchmark for existing schemes, including the exemption from the FCF job advertising requirement and COMPASS.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: What this aims to do is to set a clearer benchmark for existing schemes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will give our businesses predictability on future updates, and to ensure that our mainstream framework continues to cover the vast majority of EP applications, even as wages move up.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Pritam Singh has asked for the rationale of exempting the top 10% of EP holders from the FCF job advertising criteria and COMPASS.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For such roles, companies would already have a stringent selection process to hire the right candidate, given the impact these individuals would have on their business.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is also more likely that head-hunters or search firms will play a role to fill these jobs, and it is not typical for these roles to be filled by advertising on job portals like MyCareersFuture.sg alone.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Individuals filling these roles would also have no problems passing the COMPASS criteria given their calibre.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: However, what it does is it helps to send the right signal to global companies on our openness, by giving them greater certainty that they are able to hire their key personnel, which will make a difference to their confidence to operate here.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These global companies are a key driver in creating good jobs for locals, including opportunities for them to take on higher-level positions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And, as I will share more later, we will continue to invest heavily in developing our own local talent, so that they can compete strongly at all and every level.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Besides attracting top talent, we also want to make sure that the broad base of businesses can access complementary foreign workers, especially in areas of skills shortages.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Patrick Tay has asked whether shortening it to 14 days will remove the need for employers to exhaust all avenues to hire local PMEs, before they turn to foreign PMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Louis Chua and Mr Ang Wei Neng, have asked for more data to understand the efficacy of the FCF job advertising requirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is important for us to look at the context of when and why we increased the FCF job advertising duration to 28 days.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Based on data from MyCareerFutures.sg, the vast majority of applications are submitted within the first two weeks of a job posting – so within a fortnight.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So, 14 days was an optimal balance between giving jobseekers time to look for a job and making sure that companies could fill their vacancies in response to pressing business needs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We wanted to give local jobseekers more time to respond to job openings and employers more time to evaluate the increased number of applications.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: So, from 0.55 in June 2020, it is now in excess of 2.4.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: There are now more jobs than there are local jobseekers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But, Members of the House, make no mistake, employers are still expected to fairly consider all applicants who apply within this window.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This remains unchanged, and our employers understand this.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Last but not least, let me touch on the option of a five-year EP introduced for experienced tech professionals in areas of skills shortages.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked if this option of a five-year EP could also be extended to non-tech professionals in the sustainability sector.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For the time being, we have limited the option of a five-year EP to tech roles, for which there is an acute shortage of talent globally.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But that it is not to say that other sectors cannot benefit.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Almost all sectors require tech talent to drive transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This includes the financial services and manufacturing industries, as well as up-and-coming sustainability sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I would now like to spend some time to talk about our efforts to develop our local workforce, and in particular, our local leadership pipeline.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our policies to attract global talent are also meant to accelerate the development of our own local talent pool.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have designed our foreign workforce policies to incentivise companies to develop a strong local workforce – COMPASS, for instance, takes into account a firm’s local Professionals, Managers, Executives and Technicians (PMET) share when evaluating its EP applications.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And we will complement this with investments in our local workers, to help them succeed.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Industry Transformation Maps mapped out growth plans for 23 sectors across the economy.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For each of these 23 sectors, we have identified in-demand jobs and developed jobs and skills strategies to build up the local talent pipeline for these jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have also launched Jobs Transformation Maps, to provide job-level insights on the impact of technology on the industry and workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: With these insights, companies can redesign and enhance job roles, and equip their workers with the skills needed for these roles.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Working closely with industry and unions, the Government has spared no effort to help employers and workers to upskill and reskill for jobs of the future.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: A wide range of programmes are offered by Workforce Singapore, SkillsFuture Singapore and the various sector agencies to support training.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I echo Mr Desmond Choo, Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Lim Biow Chuan’s views on the importance of building up our local bench strength when it comes to top leadership positions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: One key priority is increasing the global and regional exposure of our local talents, so that they can take up leadership positions in global firms.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Mr Tan Wern-Yuen is an example of a Singaporean who has ventured abroad to gain valuable experience.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: He started his first overseas stint as Managing Director of McDonald's Taiwan.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: He then became the CEO of Walmart China, where he led a team of 100,000 associates responsible for over US$10 billion in annual revenue.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Now, he is back in Singapore, as CEO of PepsiCo APAC, helming the global firm’s operations across Asia Pacific, Australia, China and New Zealand.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We need more Singaporeans to do the same.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our agencies have good programmes to support this.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For instance, MAS has the Asian Financial Leaders Scheme that co-funds and sends promising Singaporeans in the Financial Services sector on leadership programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Other similar schemes include the SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative and Enterprise Singapore’s Global Ready Talent Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: At Budget this year, I also announced a new Singapore Global Executive Programme that will help local enterprises build a pipeline of young local talent with potential to take on regional or global leadership positions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Leadership development must fundamentally be driven by our businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The business community is also doing its part to nurture promising Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Singapore Business Federation (SBF) has taken the lead to form an Alliance for Action (AfA) on Business Leadership Development.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This AfA brings together businesses and local leaders to look into ways to cultivate conducive conditions for Singapore talent to strengthen regional exposure and assume key leadership roles in enterprises.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The AfA will also draw upon the diverse experiences from business and academia to help Singaporeans broaden networks and learn progressive leadership practices.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I look forward to the ideas and initiatives that the AfA will propose.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked about skills transfer as a way to build up local expertise.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Today, companies have programmes to get more experienced employees, foreign or local, to transfer skills to less experienced employees.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is in their interest to do so, for business resilience and sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They can also tap on various Government programmes, including SkillsFuture, the Enterprise Development Grant and the Capability Transfer Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Companies that set up CTCs can tap on this grant for their business and workforce transformation projects.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim has asked whether we can codify training and skills transfer requirements into law.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Some Members have previously raised the idea of time-limited EPs, as a way of ensuring skills transfer.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I would caution against too deterministic an approach.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Skills transfer is but one way that foreign manpower can contribute to Singapore and create opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In some areas, foreign manpower helps to make up the gap between demand and supply – some of these gaps can continue to persist due to local and global trends, for instance, the global lack of digital talent.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Skills transfer is another way they can make a meaningful contribution, though this can take many forms – in some cases, it would be to train up a local to take on their role.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But in others, it can be to bring in expertise in a new area, to provide leadership and to level up many more in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This includes keeping a tight labour market through regular updates to our work pass criteria, alongside significant investments to help our workforce upskill and reskill.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is also for those with outstanding achievements in arts and culture, sports, and research and academia, even if they do not meet the salary requirement.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our strategy to remain open to talent is not new – it is consistent with what other states have done in the past and in the present.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In the historical novel "Romance of the Three Kingdoms" (based largely on historical events in China), Liu Bei was able to bring together a good team because of his interest in talent and his ability to convince them to join him.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: He brought together the military generals Guan Yu and Zhang Fei, and the strategist Zhuge Liang In the battle of Red Cliff, they were able to forge an alliance with Sun Quan, to defeat the much larger Cao Cao army.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: What I want to emphasise is that Singapore is a small country and talent is our precious resource.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As a regional business hub, Singapore has always welcomed talents from diverse backgrounds to work here.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Competition for talent has intensified in the post-COVID-19 era.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We should, therefore, seize this opportunity to bring the best from around the world here to innovate and push frontiers, and increase our international competitiveness and grow our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: At the same time, we will continue to cultivate our own local talent.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have various schemes to encourage Singaporeans to go abroad to gain global and regional exposure, so that they can sharpen their global instinct, and eventually take up leadership positions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: If Singapore wants to be a global player, we need to adopt a two-pronged approach: (i) continue to bring in top talent from around the world; and (ii) continue to groom our own local talent.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Through interacting and working together with global talent, we can tap on their networks, learn from their expertise, and ultimately speed up the development of our local talent pool, and create more opportunities for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In this way, Singapore will continue to prosper, and our people can benefit from a society of ever-expanding opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: (In English): Members of the House, I have gone on at great lengths to explain the targeted nature of our recent work pass enhancements, the safeguards we will put in place and our efforts to ensure that our locals can compete fairly and strongly.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But let us never forget what our goal is, and that is, ultimately, to create opportunities for Singaporeans to grow within and benefit from.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We do not live in a zero-sum world.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Attracting and anchoring global talent in Singapore does not mean less opportunities for locals and, indeed, we have grown opportunities tremendously.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Singaporeans can pursue a wide range of careers and with vastly higher salaries.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is only possible because we have adopted a global mindset.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have welcomed global companies and global talent to our shores.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Many Singaporeans are working in or with these global companies, alongside global talent.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And the same companies often post Singaporeans abroad, giving them opportunity to develop new networks and deeper experiences.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Singapore cannot be playing a defensive game when it comes to talent.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The better we are at attracting and retaining the best talent, local and global, the higher the chances of securing our economic future and to continually be able to generate good jobs for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Conversely, if we do not do this well and we cede competitiveness to other jurisdictions, we may not even be able to hang on to our best Singaporean talent.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Ms He Ting Ru hit the nail on the head when she asked about the marketing and promotional efforts we will be putting in place.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Indeed, the ONE Pass is just a vehicle.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We will need targeted marketing and promotional efforts to get to our desired destination and to pick up the right talent, with the skillsets, networks and expertise to contribute to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In the last two weeks, I have been speaking to various parties.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Businesses have been very supportive of these moves, as it will help them to attract and retain talent in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Locals understand these moves are targeted at the top and will create more economic opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For those who are concerned with fraud and abuse, I hope my clarifications today can assure them that safeguards will be put in place.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: There is a sense that Singapore is finally emerging from the shadow of COVID-19 and that we can all work together in this next phase of growth.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We have taken an important step – to make talent all over the world sit up, pay attention and think seriously about coming to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MOM and economic agencies will continue to put in place processes to ensure the schemes are implemented well, monitor the outcomes and review the parameters as we go along.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: But it cannot just be about Government policies and compliance with rules and thresholds.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Businesses must continue to play their part to uphold fair hiring practices and promote an inclusive culture, and develop, most importantly, the Singaporean Core in their organisations and complement it with a diverse foreign workforce.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The global talent we attract must share knowledge and provide opportunities with for others including their local colleagues and outside of the workplace, to seek, to understand and respect the norms in our society.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And us locals ourselves should keep upgrading our skills and be willing to go on international stints.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: We should also help newcomers integrate into our society.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And all of us must constantly look for possibilities of what we can create together, when we bring our diverse skills and expertise, to work as one.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Let us, together, build a vibrant Singapore that is always looking to new horizons, always daring to re-invent herself and brimming with opportunities for our fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Patrick Tay, if you can keep it to two questions

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: My first question, would there be control, such that the ONE Pass does not go particularly more to those from one or two nationalities, and so that it is diverse; and whether that there will be limits on the number of dependants in which the ONE Pass holders will be able to bring in, such as children, parents, parents-in-law.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: The second question is, for family offices setting up shop in Singapore and paying their family members and relatives as employees way above the $30,000 per month salary, will they, therefore, qualify for the ONE Pass as well?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because, it is the economic agencies, together with some of the other sector agencies that we have, like MCCY, we go out through our overseas offices to look for this group of talent to bring here.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think the ability for us to diversify and ensure that it is complementary, to bring as wide a diaspora in as possible, would mitigate your concern.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It quoted a sustainability recruiter, one Greg Brittain, as saying and I quote, "The solution is not simply to import more talent.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: It needs to be a combination of upscaling and developing local talent, alongside bridging in talent to support the building of capacity within Singapore." Another individual, a Mr Dimitri Volkov of a cyber security company, remarked that only local experts can effectively identify, monitor and respond to threats and his firm contributes to the ecosystem by exposing local talent to real cyber threats.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: First, at last year's Parliamentary debate on the motion on securing Singaporeans' jobs and livelihoods, and the foreign talent policy, the Workers' Party raised several alternative proposals to alleviate the concerns of Singaporeans' at the workplace and to ensure that the local foreign employment divide does not become a permanent fault line.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: With the introduction of the ONE Pass and several changes to the Employment Pass (EP) framework, as announced by Minister, how does the Ministry intend to promote and track the transfer of skills to Singaporeans by EP holders, such as the ONE Pass?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In view of the Ministerial Statement, has the Minister ruled out fixed term employment passes or other schemes that incentivise such skills transfer to Singaporeans to address skills related underemployment, amongst other things?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Second supplementary question, MOM's press release on the ONE Pass states that there are a few routes to apply for it, and it covered two in the main text of the press release and three at the Annex.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Annex also stated that more details on the eligibility for new applications and renewals would be published.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I do not think we will cover the earlier comment on The Sunday Times.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think perhaps at a separate Sitting, I would be happy to engage him further.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In my speech earlier, I have already shared, in terms of our views about the benefits the top talent will bring in and the potential spin-offs that we have.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I suggest that he could refer to that in the Hansard.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, as we speak, there are many, many Government programmes that support capability development.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: One of the programmes that he was particularly interested in is the Capability Transfer Programme (CTP), which is one of the programmes that he has actually raised and filed Parliamentary Questions on before.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Under this CTP, funding support is provided to companies to acquire global capabilities that are not available in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This can be done in a variety of ways such as bringing foreign specialists into Singapore to train locals in new capabilities or sending locals for overseas training attachments.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our locals have experienced expanded job scopes as they acquired new skills.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The last two and a half years, we had some setbacks because of COVID-19, but with the reopening of borders, we once again would like to welcome companies to tap on this if they need to bring in global experts in cutting edge areas.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: His second point is in terms of multiple routes of the ONE Pass – ONE is an acronym for Overseas Networks & Expertise.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: More details will be released in due course.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: How will the Ministry prevent ONE Pass holders from switching jobs and joining another company at a lower salary after getting their ONE Pass?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For instance, he could primarily be engaged by one company at a salary of $30,000, but because of his skillsets in corporate governance, he could be invited to become a director on the board of another company, potentially an SME, and provide that benefit.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I do not think we should restrict that.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To his other point about renewals – it is one of those points that I raised earlier on in my speech as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will work closely with the ONE Pass holder.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will work with him regularly in terms of not just updating his progress; at the same time, we are also seeing how we can learn from the talent, the type of skillset that he has and find ways and means to continue to encourage him or her to transfer his or her skillsets to other companies or to other locals and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: And we should do more to help improve their employment opportunities as there is still a very sticky bias against this group of PMETs.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: In other words, would employers take this reduction in the advertisement period as a signal to look to foreign hires as the first resort rather than the last resort?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have shared earlier on, today, the tightness is really in businesses or employers being able to find Singaporeans to fill the jobs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We have very high job vacancies compared to jobseekers today.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think if we look at it, moving forward, it will continue to rise.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, we are almost back to where we were, as of March this year.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If you look at the refinement of all of our frameworks, the ONE Pass is really the peak – the top of the pyramid.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But over the last five to six months, we have announced an entire slew of measures as part of a balanced framework, whether it is COMPASS, we have also improved the criteria, including the qualifying salary and so on for the EP and the S Pass.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: All of that is in keeping with the development of our economy.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To the group of PMEs in the 50s and 60s, we have also offered significant support measures to ensure that they continue to stay incentivised and enfranchised to continue to work.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our Jobs Growth Incentive is one very clear example of how we have helped them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On top of that, WSG has grants to help in terms of the jobs redesign and jobs reskilling.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Parallel with that, there is also the Support for Job Redesign under Productivity Solutions Grant to help companies redesign their own job processes.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: All of these measures should be viewed not in isolation but as part of a broader objective to ensure that our Singaporeans do not get compromised at any stage.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As long as they are prepared and want to look for a job, we will be there to support them and to help them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On top of that, the Deputy Prime Minister is launching Forward SG and you know inherently in each one of the pillars, the target focus again is on Singaporeans – to see how we can continue to help them not just keep up but keep ahead of the competition.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: One of the indicators for how many Singaporeans are on track to get top jobs is how many of the good jobs advertised under the Fair Consideration Framework are given to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: The Minister has not answered my PQ as to how many of the jobs that are above $10,000 in salary per month, are filled by Singaporeans as compared to non-Singaporeans in the past five years.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: My second supplementary question: is there a maximum number of years that ONE Pass holders can have in Singapore because it will determine whether he has planned to pass on his expertise or get Singaporeans to fill the top jobs?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think it is timely that he raised this point.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As a top leader and executive himself, Mr Ang Wei Neng would appreciate the fact that at that space, people do not just rely on one portal or one scheme to get employed.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, while there are requirements for job advertisements on MyCareersFuture under the Fair Consideration Framework, many of the top talent in all the different spaces would get employment through a whole host of means.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I have also mentioned earlier on about search firms and head-hunters.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Without promoting any particular one, LinkedIn is an example.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, there are multiple ways in which people at that level can get jobs or get head-hunted.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It is for us to up the ante in terms of where we see ourselves five years, 10 years down the line, where at every part of the economy, cutting-edge, top-notch, frontier industry, we would like that talent to come to help us to launch a thousand ships in every single one of these sectors and, because of that, have spillover effects to our medium-sized, our middle segment, broaden it significantly, deepen it and allow the continued growth of our SMEs to become, eventually, local large enterprises (LLEs).

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Many SMEs, which include the small and medium audit practices or consulting practices are facing a talent crunch or manpower shortage.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I wonder can MOM extent this principle or concept to EP holders who are working in these knowledge-based industries?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Mandarin):   I agree with the Minister that we need to attract top talent like "Zhuge Liang (诸葛亮)".

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But we also need to have good training schemes to groom our own "Sima Yi (司马懿)" and "Pang Tong (庞统)".

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If I can request Members to keep their questions one language, unless you have a separate question.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I am not a fan of "Pang Tong" or "Sima Yi".

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think it is important that the Member understands that the ONE Pass is one part of a broader framework that we have been rolling out for the last few months.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, there are multiple policy refinements that we have done to ensure that we are able to differentiate and make it a lot more targeted to support the needs of the SMEs.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can the Minister share with us how MOM came to the conclusion, that the Letter of Consent (LOC) for spouses is material and needle-moving, was it based on a survey of prospective candidates or advice from an international HR consultancy?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And secondly, with this introduction of the ONE Pass, which separates the top talent from the other EP holders, it actually gives us flexibility to further adjust our EP criteria without affecting our ability to attract top talent.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, does MOM have plans to further tighten control of EP?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The feedback we get comes from multiple sources and we triangulate the data very regularly.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We get feedback from economic agencies, our own sector agencies, trade associations and also from some of the foreign chambers that we work with.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: When we talk about needle-moving initiatives like the ONE Pass, because of the segment in which we are targeting – this is the pinnacle of the pyramid that I was talking about – by sending that signal across, it signals to the world that we are open for business and that we are welcoming for talent in that very rarefied space.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And, we are prepared to bring them here, to help them set up so that we, as a country, as a people, can also benefit from their talent and their skill sets.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Earlier on, I forgot to answer a point.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Hence, my earlier statement that it will not be material, because it will not materially affect the LOCs that we are going to issue out of MOM.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that explains to the Member clearly.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: SMEs collectively employ a large majority of Singaporeans and are facing intense competition for talent to support every stage of their business growth.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I appreciate that he also shared about support for vertical sectors but I think SMEs require support every different stage of business growth and are already facing a intense competition from larger enterprises.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister, is there further direct support, direct benefits for SMEs to give them the support to find the talent that enables them to be the future large local enterprises (LLEs) and to reduce being further disadvantage in this intense competition for talent.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our intent in growing this segment, first and foremost, is targeted to improve, to increase, to broaden the spillover effects to our SMEs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have shared, we want to grow our ecosystem as a whole by creating new cheese, significantly new cheese, so that down the stream, up the stream, our local companies will benefit.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This measure will strengthen our standing as an international hub for talent.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It will bring significantly more businesses for our local companies, especially our SMEs and increase the opportunities for all of our Singaporean workers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Having said that, we have multiple grants and support solutions to continue to help strengthen and support our SMEs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We encourage our big LLEs to act as "Queen Bees" when we go out to hunt together as a pack, to bring our SMEs along.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We also hope that SMEs will work with the Government and in the multiple approaches that we have done, as we go out and expand our reach globally, we would urge the SMEs, especially our SME bosses, to be nimble.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because of their size, they are able to provide significant engaging challenges and a very responsive type of HR policies for young talent to join them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And collectively, we can build a much bigger and a much better future for all of our ecosystem here in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Together with the Singapore Business Federation, we have also supported them on the development of an Alliance for Action (AfA) to see how we can continue to help our SMEs to transform and level up.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: There are multiple measures to Mr Chia's point and we are always open to more suggestion as to how we can continue to improve our reach and our support for them.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In terms of the EPs as a whole, not just that of the top talent, in terms of meeting the FCF advertising requirements, do we have any statistical data to show that it is actually achieving its stated purpose and that companies are not just going through the motions of putting up their advertisements?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: For example, such as the number of interviews being granted or the number of applicants that actually end up being hired through these advertisements.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I recognise that as Minister shared, right now the labour market is very tight but at the same time they are actually risk in the horizon in terms of rising risk of a recession and slowing growth.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, in terms of the lower duration, would it be a bit too early to do so?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic, that was in October 2020, when we tightened the advertising period to 28 days.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We were having – our job vacancies versus the job openings was about 0.5, meaning that that there were fewer job vacancies for a lot of jobseekers.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And many companies have given feedback that they are really finding it very difficult to hire and if they wait for the period of time, for the 28-day advertising duration, they will lose the particular person that they want to hire and it compromises the operations of the business.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On top of that, we have also kept the minimum qualifying salaries for the S Pass and the EP in tandem with economic development.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I do not think that this is a wrong time.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, we are coming in from a position of strength and if the businesses cannot ramp up when they have business, when they have orders coming in and they cannot ramp up, and if the downturn happens and they get hit, I think it would be even a worse-off situation for these businesses.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Having said that I have also shared that we will not hesitate to take action if companies discriminate against locals or if they discriminate against anyone in terms of characteristics.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, in that sense, we continue to monitor the space very closely.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, to your point, rest assured, we are on top of it.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As he mentioned, Liu Bei, had to visit his friend three times to convince him to join the team.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Minister also mentioned that there will be stringent and rigorous checks to ensure the validity of the application.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Similarly, as mentioned by Mr Chia, MNCs are also facing intense challenge to attract these talents to drive transformation from Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How do we ensure the annual checks for these Pass holders can be implemented in a way that is not too onerous, so that we can continue to attract these talents, so that we can position Singapore to lead business transformation from our island?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In my speech, I have also said about giving them time to ramp up and a runway to develop and we want to encourage this group of talent to take risks, calculated risk, of course, to make sure that the payoff is significant, so that our entire economy and ecosystem benefit.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And I would also welcome Members' contributions in giving us ideas as to how we can continue to make this scheme a very sustainable and self-improving one.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I did not ask about quotas in my PQ, but instead about estimates and projections and how many are anticipated to be under ONE Pass.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I note that MOM said over the weekend that it expects about 7,000 or 8,000 to be on this new pass based on the top 5% of the EP holders.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Although of course, this scheme is meant to attract more top talent who are not already here in Singapore.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I have one clarification for the Minister and it is about the promotional activities to be carried out to promote this ONE Pass to top talent outside of Singapore.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: What is the budget and how would the success of such promotional activities be determined, when deciding whether or not we are actually getting to the right people we are hoping to attract into Singapore?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think I complimented her in my speech about the fact she got the gist of it.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think, for us, our aspiration to build a world-class ecosystem, to build a world-class talent base where we become a giant magnet to attract the best talent from all over the world to come here and contribute, I think, that in itself sends a very strong signal.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I agree with the need to bring in top talents.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, some of my residents have given me feedback about concerns with regards to the ONE Pass and how our local talent can compete fairly for opportunities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As such, I would like to ask the Minister to elaborate on how we can give assurance to local workers, especially the broad middle segment, that they can benefit from this.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Today, as I have said and they are not motherhood statements, the core of what we do, whether it is COMPASS, whether it is the ONE Pass, whether it is the raising of the minimum qualifying salaries, the local qualifying salary, everything we do, everything that Prime Minister, our Deputy Prime Ministers, Senior Ministers, all the Ministers and everyone here in this room, are focused on is that singular objective of how we can continue to provide opportunities, good pay, good career progression for our Singaporean Core.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: That is really at the core of what we do.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, to that end, we should not focus on just this ONE Pass.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The ONE Pass is about creating new cheese, new opportunities, new economic opportunities, new diaspora of different sectors for it to then spill over to our SMEs, our other local enterprises so that we can continue to provide opportunities for our Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We also have the SkillsFuture Leadership Development initiative.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: These are five very big initiatives aimed at exposing Singaporeans to leadership positions, to thought processes, thought leaders, all over the world.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because the depth, the size of our market is Singapore alone cannot give our fellow Singaporeans that necessary runway, that necessary depth to acquire the deep expertise and experience that is required.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And if there are more programmes that Members of this House do have, feel free to suggest those to us and we are prepared to consider them.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, I want to reassure all Members of the House that this is the core of what we do.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It is for our Singaporeans, our fellow Singaporeans for our future.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because 50 years later, I think many of you would still be around.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: You want to continue to see Singapore to still be brimming with opportunities, optimism and hope.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I am certain I would not be around but I am sure many of you will still be around.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that that gives you that reassurance.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think no one in this House will be against attracting more foreign talents into our country.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, if you imagine, 20 years ago, I do not know who was the Manpower Minister then.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: He would have stood there and made the same message about attracting foreign talents.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But over the last 15 to 20 years, can I ask the Minister whether we have been attracting the right kind of talents since now, 95% of the EPs currently do not meet the ONE Pass requirement.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Second question: Sir, we are very concerned and that is why we are asking many questions.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But the second point I want to make is that I support and I take the same position as the Leader of the Opposition and Workers' Party on why we cannot include mentoring skills transfer, and one more thing, I had mentioned in many of my speeches, succession planning, when we bring the talent, the foreign talent or the global talent into our market?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I ask the Minister: does it makes sense that on one hand, we pay to get the talents in —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Leong, can you keep your question succinct?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: Does it makes sense that on one hand, we pay the talents to come in to help us in capabilities transfer but, on the other hand, we have a lot of talents that are working in Singapore and they opt to work in Singapore and we did not make it a requirement to renew their visa?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To his first point, 20 years ago, if I may just use one example and that is the example that the Prime Minister delivered in the National Day Rally when he talked about the entire biomedical industry; and he also mentioned Mr Philip Yeo, who went out there, brought the whales in to Singapore and developed our own biomedical enterprise.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think that Mr Leong himself would have benefited from the PCR testing.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At some stage, he may have used the Fortitude test kits.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: That came out of a homegrown enterprise, a company called MiRXES.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It was a spin-off from the entire biomedical industry that Prime Minister talked about during the National Day Rally.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, I do not think I need to dwell on that.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I can go on with multiple examples to showcase to him that indeed, from where we have started to where we are today, we have certainly benefited from the global talent coming here with the transfers of skillsets, capabilities, knowledge and so on and so forth.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To his second point in terms of succession planning and so on, I think we are now at the stage where we are not only looking at skillsets, expertise alone, more so than the proxy of the $30,000-mark, we are looking at creating a significantly different ecosystem, one that will hopefully ensure our continued prosperity and progress for the next five or 10 decades and beyond.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I am very optimistic that in subsequent Parliamentary Sittings, there will be opportunity for the Member to continue to raise this type of questions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Many countries have made changes to their talent policies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: UAE has the Golden Visa, UK and Germany have introduced new passes to attract talent.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Then, we are going after those sectors where we are going to be able to create new cheese for ourselves and with that new cheese, provide significant economic opportunities to benefit our entire ecosystem of the SMEs and raising up our Singapore Core.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, to that end, that is what we are focused on today.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To go beyond identifying different sectors and so on, would also compromise our ability to ramp up and to upscale.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And as I have shared in my interview with Bloomberg, I do not want to start a bidding war.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that addresses Mr Desmond Choo's points.
